name: Non-hereditary Congenital Primary Lymphedema

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Lymphedema

criteria.description: Onset of lymphedema at birth or within the first two years of life
No family history of lymphedema or related lymphatic disorders
Presence of non-pitting edema predominantly affecting lower limbs
Lymphoscintigraphy or MR lymphangiography demonstrating lymphatic hypoplasia or aplasia
Exclusion of secondary causes of lymphedema such as infection, trauma, or malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital onset lymphedema with no family history and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing typically negative for known hereditary lymphedema mutations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital non-pitting lymphedema of lower extremities
pathognomonic.notes: Typically unilateral or bilateral swelling present at birth or early infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lymphatic hypoplasia or aplasia confirmed by imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Demonstrated by lymphoscintigraphy or MR lymphangiography

common.symptomName: Skin thickening and fibrosis over affected limbs
common.notes: Progressive skin changes due to chronic lymphatic stasis
searchTerms: skin thickening and hardening on limbs
tightened skin over affected arms or legs

common.notes: Inability to pinch skin at base of second toe or finger
searchTerms: skin fold cannot be pinched at toe

common.notes: Secondary infections due to impaired lymphatic drainage

occasional.notes: Thickened, scaly skin in chronic cases

occasional.symptomName: Limited joint mobility due to limb swelling
occasional.notes: Stiffness or decreased range of motion in affected limb joints
searchTerms: limited limb mobility due to edema

occasional.notes: One limb may be larger than the other
searchTerms: mild asymmetry of arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue or heaviness in affected limb
searchTerms: feeling tired or heavy in one limb
heaviness sensation in affected arm or leg

rare.notes: Rare vesicular lesions due to lymphatic vessel dilation
Very rare malignant transformation in chronic lymphedema

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during cellulitis episodes
imaging: Lymphoscintigraphy showing lymphatic hypoplasia or aplasia
MR lymphangiography demonstrating lymphatic vessel abnormalities
genetic: Absence of mutations in known hereditary lymphedema genes (e.g., FLT4, FOXC2)
other: Exclusion of secondary causes by history and examination

distinguishingFeatures: History of infection, trauma, surgery, or malignancy

redFlags: Signs of infection such as fever and erythema
Development of skin ulceration or lymphangiosarcoma
references: Mellor RH, et al. Primary lymphedema: clinical features and genetic insights. J Vasc Surg. 2020.
International Society of Lymphology. The diagnosis and treatment of peripheral lymphedema: 2020 Consensus Document.
